title: Decide whether another generation is worth it

cards.summary: When the first candidate meets the user request and only incidental or unverifiable details remain, finish with it; named user details are not incidental.
cards.section: S1 · Finish when the first candidate already meets the core request

cards.summary: Before another Bernini attempt, weigh the specific gain against already-passing requirements; finish when the remaining gain is only incidental.
cards.section: S2 · A later attempt is a risk, not a free retry

cards.summary: If a core requirement is unmet, try an omitted instruction, a different realization or a better-supported input; stop when no consequential new hypothesis remains.
cards.section: S3 · Continue only with a concrete, untried reason

cards.summary: When a review lists many partial findings, distinguish user requirements and major damage from incidental details before deciding to generate again.
cards.status: observed (2) · applies to the current online Critic version
cards.section: S4 · Read online reviews by importance, not by verdict count

cards.summary: After two targeted attempts leave an explicit requirement unrealized, stop repeating that realization; try again only for a materially different mechanism.
cards.section: S5 · Stop repeating a method with low expected benefit

cards.summary: When finishing, state the stop reason and consequential unresolved issues; unused budget does not require another attempt.
cards.section: S6 · Finish honestly

title: Respond to an unmet requirement by its failure type

cards.summary: When a failure diagnosis changes the proposed action, distinguish omission, binding failure, inherited loss and introduced damage; overlapping causes are allowed.
cards.section: R1 · Use failure distinctions when they clarify the action

cards.summary: If the prompt omitted a requested visible relation, state that relation explicitly in the next realization.
cards.section: R2 · Omitted → state the wanted visible state explicitly

cards.summary: If an explicit request was not realized, change how the visual result is produced instead of merely increasing verbal emphasis.
cards.status: mixed · recurring observations across two renderers; the stopping policy is unvalidated
cards.section: R3 · Prefer a different realization over stronger emphasis after explicit failure

cards.summary: When correcting an unwanted attribute, describe the desired visible state rather than repeating a list of unwanted attributes.
cards.status: mixed → treat as a strong default
cards.section: R4 · Prefer wanted states over lists of unwanted attributes

cards.summary: If the latest attempt introduced consequential damage, consider an earlier input without that damage before asking the damaged candidate to undo it.
cards.section: R5 · Introduced regression → go back to an input without it

cards.summary: If identity information disappeared, return to conditioning that retains it or reduce the conflicting transformation; naming facial details did not reliably restore it.
cards.section: R6 · Naming lost identity is a weak reconstruction strategy

cards.summary: If an authored addition occludes or contradicts preserved structure, remove or redesign that addition rather than adding preservation clauses.
cards.section: R7 · Drop authored additions that collide with preserved structure

cards.summary: For a compatible environmental addition or texture extension, build on a candidate that already supplies the desired treatment and necessary scene information.
cards.section: I1 · Continue a candidate for additive or texture changes

cards.summary: For precise Ditto shape correction on a candidate, prefer a usable approximation or source-based alternative; recorded edits added or retained the wrong geometry.
cards.section: I2 · Lower expectations for precise geometry repair on a candidate

cards.summary: Restart from source when it contains information the proposed fix needs, and change the realization that lost it; reusing the same design repeats the risk.
cards.status: mixed; route and realization changed together
cards.section: I3 · Restart from the source only when the source has what the fix needs

cards.summary: If a later candidate gained a defect absent from an earlier useful candidate, branch from the earlier candidate.
cards.section: I4 · Branch from an earlier candidate to escape a regression

cards.summary: Choose an editing input for the information the next change needs; keep the best delivery candidate separately available.
cards.section: I5 · The best delivery and the best input can differ

title: Express an edit for its actual input

cards.summary: When specifying an edit, describe the desired visible state; negative attribute lists may reintroduce the unwanted appearance.
cards.section: X1 · Describe wanted states, not prohibitions

cards.summary: For a broad short style request, express its visible medium, surface and lighting relations without inventing new narrative requirements.
cards.section: X2 · Make a short style request concrete

cards.summary: When an effect belongs to a part, bind it to that part and its surrounding contrast; a named property can otherwise land on a neighboring structure.
cards.section: X3 · Bind local effects to the part, and say what stays unlit

cards.summary: When preserving a person, reduce transformations that conflict with identity-bearing regions; more facial description is not a reliable identity lock.
cards.section: X4 · Do not try to preserve a person by describing them

cards.summary: When specifying a small landmark, bind its position and scale to the scene; a strong object noun may invite a new enlarged instance.
cards.section: X5 · Refer to small landmarks by place and size, not by a strong noun

cards.summary: When revising a scene, describe a coherent visual field and realization; verbal smallness does not create a spatial mask.
cards.section: X6 · Keep each revision's scope coherent

cards.summary: When extending a prompt, add useful visual relations or resolve ambiguity; added length alone did not ensure semantic preservation.
cards.section: X7 · Longer is not better on its own

cards.summary: When selecting delivery, prioritize the user requirements and consequential damage, then compare the remaining appearance tradeoffs.
cards.section: C1 · Select by core requirements and major damage first

cards.summary: Before selecting among plausible contenders, compare their actual evidence, including an earlier candidate that still has a relevant advantage.
cards.section: C2 · Compare every real contender before finishing

cards.summary: Before spending a generation on a consequential but uncertain review claim, inspect the relevant video evidence when it could change the decision.
cards.section: C3 · Check a consequential claim yourself before spending a generation

cards.summary: When a judgment is unknown, retain the uncertainty and seek relevant evidence if worthwhile; do not treat it as a confirmed defect.
cards.section: C4 · Unknown is not failure

cards.summary: If a Bernini short-style candidate already meets the request, finish rather than spend another sample repairing incidental structure.
If Bernini leaves the environment partly unchanged, consider a compatible addition from a useful candidate; complete replacement was unreliable on the recorded source.
If Bernini places an effect on the wrong part, try a different binding or realization once; repeating emphasis has weak support.
If a Bernini transformation damages identity, reduce the conflicting treatment near identity-bearing regions; extra identity descriptions did not reliably repair it.
If Bernini leaves explicit displacement unrealized, stop wording-only retries after repeated failure; a different visible realization remains testable.
When orientation or pose matters in Bernini, state that relation in the initial prompt; correcting an omitted orientation succeeded in the recorded task.
If a Bernini close-up shows expression drift, weigh it against the actual request before another generation; descriptive preservation may not fix it.
If a Ditto candidate already meets the core request without consequential damage, finish instead of chasing incidental detail.
If Ditto already replaces the environment strongly, focus the next decision on preservation tradeoffs instead of strengthening the replacement again.
If Ditto changes faces, age or glasses during a strong edit, reconsider the conflicting transformation and input; descriptive identity constraints were insufficient.
If Ditto ignores a requested silhouette change, prefer another realization over wording-only repair; one failed example does not establish incapability.
For neutral face lighting in Ditto, describe neutral illumination positively; repeating the unwanted color during correction increased it in the recorded case.
If a Ditto candidate has wrong object geometry, consider another input or retain a useful approximation; candidate-based correction created a second dome in the recorded case.
When Ditto applies an etching style, inspect landmark scale and added architectural elements before accepting the result.
If Ditto leaves an explicit effect unrealized repeatedly, stop repeating the same wording and report the remaining gap or test a new realization.
When subject orientation matters in Ditto, state it explicitly; adding the omitted back-facing relation corrected the recorded task.
